# What should you do when you are left on read? How to think it through before you send a follow-up

The message was seen. The read receipt is there. And then — nothing. An hour passes, then an evening, and your thumb starts composing a second message you are not sure you should send. We built Honne, our iPhone chat-analysis app, for exactly this pause. Its App Store description puts it plainly: paste a dry text or a left-on-read chat, see what the other person might mean, and get a reply that will not make things worse. This guide explains how we think through a left-on-read moment ourselves, what Honne can and cannot do in it, and what our own measured numbers say about the app so far.

## Why does being left on read feel so loud?

A read receipt removes the easiest explanation — "they probably have not seen it yet" — and replaces it with silence you have to interpret yourself. The problem is that the silence carries almost no information. The same unanswered message can mean a busy afternoon, a phone left in another room, a reply that needs thought, or a conversation the other person does not want to continue. Which of those you believe usually depends less on the message than on the relationship: an unanswered text from a partner at midnight feels different from an unanswered text from a colleague on a workday afternoon.

That is why the first step in Honne is not the message at all. It is the relationship.

## How do you use Honne for a left-on-read chat?

The flow is the same three steps we document on the [Honne product page](/honne), and it takes less than a minute:

1. **Choose the relationship.** Partner or couple, friend, family, or colleague or boss. A silence means something different inside each of those, and the reading should start from the widest context you actually have.
2. **Paste the message.** Bring in the last part of the chat — what you sent and what came before it. Leave out names and other personal details that are not needed for the reading. On the App Store listing we state that the developer does not collect data from this app, and the current version is 1.0.7 (checked on the US App Store on 13 November 2026).
3. **Review the interpretation and the suggested reply.** Honne shows possible readings of the tone — the listing describes it as looking for the emotions behind the words, such as anger, anxiety, loneliness, or hope — together with a suggested response. Treat the reading as a list of possibilities to weigh, not as a verdict, and rewrite the suggestion until it sounds like you.

You can run three analyses a day for free. Premium removes the daily limit and adds unlimited analyses, full history, priority speed, and deeper insights. On the US App Store the Premium plans are listed at $7.99 weekly, $14.99 monthly, and $49.99 annually (checked 13 November 2026; prices are shown in your region before you buy). Honne requires iOS 18 or later on iPhone, is listed in English, and is 19.3 MB.

## Should you send a follow-up at all?

Before drafting anything, we ask three questions, in this order.

**Did your message actually need an answer?** A photo, a reaction, or a "sounds good" often closes a thread by design. Not every seen message is an unanswered question.

**How much time has really passed, for them?** Your waiting time and their available time are different clocks. Work hours, sleep, travel, and family time all sit between a read receipt and a reply, and none of them are visible to you.

**What would a follow-up add?** A follow-up that adds new information — a deadline, a choice, an easy way to say no — is a different message from a follow-up that only repeats "did you see this?". If you do send one, send the first kind: short, specific, and easy to answer. That is also the standard we hold Honne's reply suggestions to: keep what fits, change what does not, and never send wording you would not say out loud.

## What do our measured numbers say about Honne so far?

We publish our numbers as measured, with the period and the source, even when they are small. The figures below are from App Store Connect, measured on 13 November 2026.

In the 28 days from 15 October to 11 November 2026, Honne recorded 2,346 impressions, 91 product page views, and 13 downloads — 12 in Japan and 1 in Germany. The downloads came from App Store search (5), App Store browse (4), web referrers (3), and app referrers (1). In the most recent 7 days of that window, 5 to 11 November, there were 141 impressions, 5 product page views, and no downloads. As of 11 November 2026, two people held an active paid subscription.

We read that honestly: people are finding the page, a small number are installing, and the recent week shows the funnel can stall completely. A guide like this one is part of our answer — being present, with a careful explanation, at the exact moment someone searches for help with a message they cannot read. If you are in that moment now, the free tier is enough to try the reading once, on the chat that is actually bothering you.

## What should you not use Honne for?

Honne offers interpretations, not facts about another person's feelings, and a plausible reading can still be wrong. A read receipt cannot tell you why someone has not replied, and neither can an AI. If the conversation is urgent, serious, or about safety, contact the person directly — or through another channel — instead of analysing their silence. And because you are pasting real conversations, leave out names and details the reading does not need.

## Common questions

### Is Honne free to use?

Yes. You can run three analyses per day for free. Premium adds unlimited analyses, full history, priority speed, and deeper insights, at $7.99 weekly, $14.99 monthly, or $49.99 annually on the US App Store (checked 13 November 2026).

### Does the other person know I analysed their message?

No. You paste the text yourself inside Honne; the other person is not notified, as we state on the App Store listing.

### Can Honne tell me why someone left me on read?

No. It can show possible readings of the chat and help you draft a calmer follow-up, but the reason for a silence is something only the sender knows. If the meaning matters, ask them.

### Which devices and languages does Honne support?

Honne requires iOS 18 or later on iPhone (iPadOS 18 or later on iPad) and is listed in English on the App Store, in the Utilities category.

### Where can I get Honne?

On the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759667221), and you can read more on the [Honne product page](/honne). If your problem is a short reply rather than a silence, start with our companion guide, [What does this text mean?](/blog/honne-what-does-this-text-mean), and browse the rest of the series on the [Honne blog hub](/blog/c/honne).
